# hexf_parse - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/hexf-parse/

## Expand description

Parses hexadecimal float literals.
There are two functions `parse_hexf32` and `parse_hexf64` provided for each type.

```
use hexf_parse::*;
assert_eq!(parse_hexf32("0x1.99999ap-4", false), Ok(0.1f32));
assert_eq!(parse_hexf64("0x1.999999999999ap-4", false), Ok(0.1f64));
```
An additional `bool` parameter can be set to true if you want to allow underscores.

```
use hexf_parse::*;
assert!(parse_hexf64("0x0.1_7p8", false).is_err());
assert_eq!(parse_hexf64("0x0.1_7p8", true), Ok(23.0f64));
```
The error is reported via an opaque `ParseHexfError` type.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseHexfError.html)- Hexf - Error
- An opaque error type from `parse_hexf32`and`parse_hexf64`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_hexf32.html)- hexf32
- Tries to parse a hexadecimal float literal to `f32`. The underscore is allowed only when`allow_underscore`is true.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_hexf64.html)- hexf64
- Tries to parse a hexadecimal float literal to `f64`. The underscore is allowed only when`allow_underscore`is true.

---

use hexf_parse::*;

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Badges

Source: https://docs.rs/about/badges

Docs.rs no longer has its own badges. Consider using [shields.io](https://shields.io) instead.

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# smooth_operator_adapter_memory - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-adapter-memory/1.11.1/smooth_operator_adapter_memory/

## Expand description

In-memory [ StorageAdapter](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/adapter/trait.StorageAdapter.html) — the conformance / test baseline.

All OLTP slices (conversations, participants, messages, sessions) live in
`HashMap`s behind a single `RwLock`. The checkpoint and knowledge slices
delegate to smooth-operator’s own [ MemoryCheckpointStore](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/checkpoint/struct.MemoryCheckpointStore.html) and

[, which are exactly what the engine expects — so this adapter is a faithful (if non-durable) stand-in for Postgres/DynamoDB.](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/knowledge/struct.InMemoryKnowledge.html)

`InMemoryKnowledge`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [InMemory](https://docs.rs/struct.InMemoryStorageAdapter.html)- Storage - Adapter
- In-memory storage adapter. Cheap to clone is *not*a goal — wrap in`Arc`for sharing.

# smooth_operator_ingestion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-ingestion/1.11.1/smooth_operator_ingestion/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#smooth-operator-ingestion)smooth-operator ingestion

Knowledge **ingestion + connectors** for smooth-operator — the pipeline
that pulls documents from a source, chunks them, embeds them, and stores them
in the [ StorageAdapter](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/adapter/trait.StorageAdapter.html)
knowledge slice so they are retrievable. This closes feature gap G1 (knowledge
ingestion + connectors), G2 (document chunking pipeline), and G9 (the
connector mock +

`unit`-vs-`external` test split). See `docs/INGESTION.md`.[§](https://docs.rs#shape)Shape

```
Connector::pull ─▶ Chunker::chunk ─▶ Embedder::embed ─▶ KnowledgeBase::ingest
   RawDocument        Vec<Chunk>        Vec<Vec<f32>>        (StorageAdapter
                                                              knowledge slice)
```
- `Connector`- `RawDocument`- `pull(since)`). Built-ins:- `FileConnector`- `WebConnector`- `MockConnector`
- `Chunker`
- `Embedder`- `smooth_operator::embedding`- `DeterministicEmbedder`
- `ingest`- `(doc id, content hash)`via an- `IngestLedger`

[§](https://docs.rs#wiring-example)Wiring example

```
let connector = FileConnector::new("./docs");
let report = ingest(
    &connector,
    &Chunker::default(),
    &DeterministicEmbedder::new(),
    storage.knowledge(),
    IngestOptions::for_org("org-acme"),
)
.await?;
println!("stored {} chunks", report.chunks_stored);
```

input string, each of length `Embedder::dim`

# smooth_operator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#smooth-operator)smooth-operator

The reference core for smooth-operator — the service layer on top of
[ smooth_operator_core](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/index.html) (the agent engine). It defines three things:

- `domain`- `spec/domain/*.json`. Checkpoints re-use the engine’s- `smooth_operator_core::Checkpoint`
- `adapter`- `StorageAdapter`- `docs/STORAGE.md`). Its checkpoint/knowledge accessors return smooth-operator-core’s own traits so the engine plugs straight in.
- `runtime`- `AgentRuntime`- `Agent`- `Workflow`

It also owns two shared retrieval seams both backends/consumers depend on:
[ embedding](https://docs.rs/embedding/index.html) (the text→vector

[+ the network-free](https://docs.rs/embedding/trait.Embedder.html)

`Embedder`[, the one home for both the Postgres adapter and the ingestion pipeline) and](https://docs.rs/embedding/struct.DeterministicEmbedder.html)

`DeterministicEmbedder`[(the optional post-retrieval](https://docs.rs/rerank/index.html)

`rerank`[stage — feature gap G8).](https://docs.rs/rerank/trait.Reranker.html)

`Reranker`## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [access_](https://docs.rs/access_control/index.html)- control
- Document-level access control (feature gap G3).
- [adapter](https://docs.rs/adapter/index.html)
- The `StorageAdapter`seam.
- [agent_](https://docs.rs/agent_config/index.html)- config
- Per-agent behavior config (SMOODEV-590 parity in Rust).
- [auth](https://docs.rs/auth/index.html)
- Authentication + role-based access control (Phase 12).
- [backplane](https://docs.rs/backplane/index.html)
- Connection backplane: the scale-out + event-delivery seam for the WebSocket server.
- [connector_](https://docs.rs/connector_config/index.html)- config
- Connector configuration storage (Phase 12, increment 3).
- [curation](https://docs.rs/curation/index.html)
- Document sets, curation boosting, and query-time metadata filters (feature gap, Phase 11 — “Document sets / curation / boosting”).
- [domain](https://docs.rs/domain/index.html)
- Domain model for smooth-operator.
- [embedding](https://docs.rs/embedding/index.html)
- Text → vector embedding — the shared seam for dense retrieval.
- [gateway_](https://docs.rs/gateway_key/index.html)- key
- Per-org LLM gateway-key resolution: the seam that lets a multi-tenant
deployment bill/scope each org’s turns to its **own**gateway key while a standalone/local server keeps using the single environment key.
- [otp](https://docs.rs/otp/index.html)
- End-user identity verification (OTP) — the seam that lets a host wire a
one-time-code flow behind a public agent’s `end_user`tool auth, while the reference server stays credential-free.
- [rerank](https://docs.rs/rerank/index.html)
- Reranking — the optional post-retrieval reorder stage (feature gap G8).
- [runtime](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html)
- Minimal `AgentRuntime`that proves smooth-operator consumes smooth-operator.
- [settings](https://docs.rs/settings/index.html)
- Per-org agent settings storage (Phase 12, increment 3).
- [telemetry](https://docs.rs/telemetry/index.html)
- OpenTelemetry GenAI instrumentation for the agent turn.
- [tool_](https://docs.rs/tool_provider/index.html)- provider
- Host-contributed tool injection seam.
- [tools](https://docs.rs/tools/index.html)
- Tools the smooth-operator runtime registers on the smooth-operator-core engine.
- [widget_](https://docs.rs/widget_auth/index.html)- auth
- Embeddable-widget auth: an origin allowlist + public-key `authContext`verification for browser-embedded chat widgets (`<smooth-agent-chat>`).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Checkpoint](https://docs.rs/struct.Checkpoint.html)
- A checkpoint captures the full state of an agent at a point in time.

# stop - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/stop-cli/0.0.2/stop/

## Expand description

Process and system monitoring with structured output.

Provides cross-platform system metrics collection with filtering, sorting, and multiple output formats (JSON, CSV, human-readable).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [data](https://docs.rs/data/index.html)
- Data types and collection for system snapshots.

- Error types for the stop CLI tool.

- Filter expression parsing and evaluation for process queries.

- Process filtering pipeline: search → filter → sort → truncate.
- [watch](https://docs.rs/watch/index.html)
- Continuous monitoring (watch mode).

- [SetPsm](https://docs.rs/struct.SetPsmStorageVersionV2.html)- Storage - Version - V2
- One-shot migration: writes `pallet_psm`’s on-chain storage version to v2. Required because`RemovePallet<PsmName>`(above in the migration tuple) wipes the pallet’s`:__STORAGE_VERSION__:`key, and`InitializePsm`doesn’t re-seed it. Without this, try-runtime’s post-upgrade check sees in-code = 2, on-chain = 0 and panics.

# masl_formatter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/masl_formatter/1.0.0/masl_formatter/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#masl_formatter)masl_formatter

Canonical source code formatter for `.mdk` files.

Consumes an `masl_ast::Document` and produces formatted MASL source text.
Never modifies semantics. Guarantees idempotency: fmt(fmt(S)) == fmt(S).

See RFC-0019 — Formatter.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [format](https://docs.rs/fn.format.html)
- Format a parsed AST Document back to canonical MASL source text.

- Type of resumption behavior on the server side.
- [Status](https://docs.rs/enum.StatusCode.html)- Code
- Enum of quic status codes.
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/enum.StreamEvent.html)- Event
- Stream callback events
- [TlsProvider](https://docs.rs/enum.TlsProvider.html)
- The different possible TLS providers used by MsQuic.

# aipmc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/aipmc/0.0.1/aipmc/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#aipmc-aip-%E6%99%BA%E8%83%BD%E4%BD%93%E4%BA%92%E8%81%94%E5%8D%8F%E8%AE%AE-mcu-%E5%AE%9E%E7%8E%B0)aipmc: AIP 智能体互联协议 MCU 实现

本 crate 是 AIPMC 项目的统一导出层，将所有子模块重新导出，
用户只需引入 `aipmc` 即可使用完整的协议栈功能。

[§](https://docs.rs#%E5%AD%90%E6%A8%A1%E5%9D%97)子模块

| 模块 | crate | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `basic` | aipmc-basic | 核心协议库（协议/消息/编解码） |
| `transport` | aipmc-transport | 传输层（UART/WiFi/BLE） |
| [ `esp32`] | aipmc-esp32 | ESP-32 平台适配（需 feature） |
| [ `stm32`] | aipmc-stm32 | STM-32 平台适配（需 feature） |

[§](https://docs.rs#%E4%BD%BF%E7%94%A8%E7%A4%BA%E4%BE%8B)使用示例

```
use aipmc::basic::{AgentCard, AgentSkill, AcpMessage, AcpMethod, AgentCapability};
let agent = AgentCard::new("dev-01", "MyAgent", "A test agent")
    .unwrap()
    .with_capability(AgentCapability::SensorRead)
    .unwrap()
    .with_skill(AgentSkill::new("temp", "ReadTemp", "Read temperature").unwrap())
    .unwrap();
let msg = AcpMessage::with_payload(AcpMethod::Initialize, 0, b"hello").unwrap();
let encoded = msg.encode().unwrap();
let decoded = AcpMessage::decode(&encoded).unwrap();
assert_eq!(decoded.session_id, 0);
```

---

# aipmc_stm32 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/aipmc-stm32/0.0.1/aipmc_stm32/

[§](#aipmc-stm32-aip-%E6%99%BA%E8%83%BD%E4%BD%93%E4%BA%92%E8%81%94%E5%8D%8F%E8%AE%AE-stm-32-%E5%B9%B3%E5%8F%B0%E9%80%82%E9%85%8D%E5%B1%82)aipmc-stm32: AIP 智能体互联协议 STM-32 平台适配层

提供 STM-32 系列芯片的硬件抽象层（HAL），封装 UART/SPI 初始化、
GPIO 控制等平台特定功能，使上层协议栈无需关注硬件细节。

[§](#%E6%94%AF%E6%8C%81%E7%9A%84%E8%8A%AF%E7%89%87%E7%B3%BB%E5%88%97)支持的芯片系列

| Feature | 芯片系列 |
|---|
| `stm32f4` | STM32F4xx |
| `stm32h7` | STM32H7xx |
| `stm32l4` | STM32L4xx |
| `stm32g4` | STM32G4xx |

[§](#%E5%BD%93%E5%89%8D%E7%8A%B6%E6%80%81)当前状态

骨架实现，待对接 `stm32-hal` 后完善。

# hexf-parse 0.2.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/hexf-parse/0.2.1

Parses hexadecimal float literals.
There are two functions `parse_hexf32` and `parse_hexf64` provided for each type.

```
use *;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
An additional `bool` parameter can be set to true if you want to allow underscores.

```
use *;
assert!;
assert_eq!;
```
The error is reported via an opaque `ParseHexfError` type.

# hexf_parse - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/hexf-parse/0.2.1/target-redirect/hexf_parse/

## Expand description

Parses hexadecimal float literals.
There are two functions `parse_hexf32` and `parse_hexf64` provided for each type.

```
use hexf_parse::*;
assert_eq!(parse_hexf32("0x1.99999ap-4", false), Ok(0.1f32));
assert_eq!(parse_hexf64("0x1.999999999999ap-4", false), Ok(0.1f64));
```
An additional `bool` parameter can be set to true if you want to allow underscores.

```
use hexf_parse::*;
assert!(parse_hexf64("0x0.1_7p8", false).is_err());
assert_eq!(parse_hexf64("0x0.1_7p8", true), Ok(23.0f64));
```
The error is reported via an opaque `ParseHexfError` type.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseHexfError.html)- Hexf - Error
- An opaque error type from `parse_hexf32`and`parse_hexf64`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_hexf32.html)- hexf32
- Tries to parse a hexadecimal float literal to `f32`. The underscore is allowed only when`allow_underscore`is true.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_hexf64.html)- hexf64
- Tries to parse a hexadecimal float literal to `f64`. The underscore is allowed only when`allow_underscore`is true.

---

```
use hexf_parse::*;

[26](#26)}
[27](#27)
[28](#28)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
[29](#29)enum ParseHexfErrorKind {
[30](#30)    Empty,
[31](#31)    Invalid,
[32](#32)    Inexact,
[33](#33)}
[34](#34)
[35](#35)const EMPTY: ParseHexfError = ParseHexfError {
[36](#36)    kind: ParseHexfErrorKind::Empty,
[37](#37)};
[38](#38)const INVALID: ParseHexfError = ParseHexfError {
[39](#39)    kind: ParseHexfErrorKind::Invalid,
[40](#40)};
[41](#41)const INEXACT: ParseHexfError = ParseHexfError {
[42](#42)    kind: ParseHexfErrorKind::Inexact,
[43](#43)};
[44](#44)
[45](#45)impl ParseHexfError {
[46](#46)    fn text(&self) -> &'static str {
[47](#47)        match self.kind {
[48](#48)            ParseHexfErrorKind::Empty => "cannot parse float from empty string",
[49](#49)            ParseHexfErrorKind::Invalid => "invalid hexadecimal float literal",
[50](#50)            ParseHexfErrorKind::Inexact => "cannot exactly represent float in target type",
[51](#51)        }
[52](#52)    }
[53](#53)}
[54](#54)
[55](#55)impl fmt::Display for ParseHexfError {
[56](#56)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
[57](#57)        fmt::Display::fmt(self.text(), f)
[58](#58)    }
[59](#59)}
[60](#60)
[61](#61)impl std::error::Error for ParseHexfError {
[62](#62)    fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
[63](#63)        self.text()
[64](#64)    }
[65](#65)}
[66](#66)
[67](#67)fn parse(s: &[u8], allow_underscore: bool) -> Result<(bool, u64, isize), ParseHexfError> {
[68](#68)    let (s, negative) = match s.split_first() {
[70](#70)        Some((&b'+', s)) => (s, false),
[71](#71)        Some((&b'-', s)) => (s, true),
[72](#72)        Some(_) => (s, false),
[73](#73)        None => return Err(EMPTY),
[74](#74)    };
[75](#75)
[76](#76)    if !(s.starts_with(b"0x") || s.starts_with(b"0X")) {
[78](#78)        return Err(INVALID);
[79](#79)    }
[80](#80)
[81](#81)    let mut s = &s[2..];
[83](#83)    let mut acc = 0; let mut digit_seen = false;
[85](#85)    loop {
[86](#86)        let (s_, digit) = match s.split_first() {
[87](#87)            Some((&c @ b'0'..=b'9', s)) => (s, c - b'0'),
[88](#88)            Some((&c @ b'a'..=b'f', s)) => (s, c - b'a' + 10),
[89](#89)            Some((&c @ b'A'..=b'F', s)) => (s, c - b'A' + 10),
[90](#90)            Some((&b'_', s_)) if allow_underscore && digit_seen => {
[91](#91)                s = s_;
[92](#92)                continue;
[93](#93)            }
[94](#94)            _ => break,
[95](#95)        };
[96](#96)
[97](#97)        s = s_;
[98](#98)        digit_seen = true;
[99](#99)
[100](#100)        if acc >> 60 != 0 {
[102](#102)            return Err(INEXACT);
[103](#103)        }
[104](#104)        acc = acc << 4 | digit as u64;
[105](#105)    }
[106](#106)
[107](#107)    let mut nfracs = 0isize; let mut nzeroes = 0isize;
[112](#112)    let mut frac_digit_seen = false;
[113](#113)    if s.starts_with(b".") {
[114](#114)        s = &s[1..];
[115](#115)        loop {
[116](#116)            let (s_, digit) = match s.split_first() {
[117](#117)                Some((&c @ b'0'..=b'9', s)) => (s, c - b'0'),
[118](#118)                Some((&c @ b'a'..=b'f', s)) => (s, c - b'a' + 10),
[119](#119)                Some((&c @ b'A'..=b'F', s)) => (s, c - b'A' + 10),
[120](#120)                Some((&b'_', s_)) if allow_underscore && frac_digit_seen => {
[121](#121)                    s = s_;
[122](#122)                    continue;
[123](#123)                }
[124](#124)                _ => break,
[125](#125)            };
[126](#126)
[127](#127)            s = s_;
[128](#128)            frac_digit_seen = true;
[129](#129)
[130](#130)            if digit == 0 {
[131](#131)                nzeroes = nzeroes.checked_add(1).ok_or(INEXACT)?;
[132](#132)            } else {
[133](#133)                let nnewdigits = nzeroes.checked_add(1).ok_or(INEXACT)?;
[135](#135)                nfracs = nfracs.checked_add(nnewdigits).ok_or(INEXACT)?;
[136](#136)                nzeroes = 0;
[137](#137)
[138](#138)                if acc != 0 {
[142](#142)                    if nnewdigits >= 16 || acc >> (64 - nnewdigits * 4) != 0 {
[143](#143)                        return Err(INEXACT);
[144](#144)                    }
[145](#145)                    acc = acc << (nnewdigits * 4);
[146](#146)                }
[147](#147)                acc |= digit as u64;
[148](#148)            }
[149](#149)        }
[150](#150)    }
[151](#151)
[152](#152)    if !(digit_seen || frac_digit_seen) {
[154](#154)        return Err(INVALID);
[155](#155)    }
[156](#156)
[157](#157)    let s = match s.split_first() {
[159](#159)        Some((&b'P', s)) | Some((&b'p', s)) => s,
[160](#160)        _ => return Err(INVALID),
[161](#161)    };
[162](#162)
[163](#163)    let (mut s, negative_exponent) = match s.split_first() {
[165](#165)        Some((&b'+', s)) => (s, false),
[166](#166)        Some((&b'-', s)) => (s, true),
[167](#167)        Some(_) => (s, false),
[168](#168)        None => return Err(INVALID),
[169](#169)    };
[170](#170)
[171](#171)    let mut digit_seen = false;
[173](#173)    let mut exponent = 0isize; loop {
[175](#175)        let (s_, digit) = match s.split_first() {
[176](#176)            Some((&c @ b'0'..=b'9', s)) => (s, c - b'0'),
[177](#177)            Some((&b'_', s_)) if allow_underscore => {
[178](#178)                s = s_;
[179](#179)                continue;
[180](#180)            }
[181](#181)            None if digit_seen => break,
[182](#182)            _ => return Err(INVALID),
[184](#184)        };
[185](#185)
[186](#186)        s = s_;
[187](#187)        digit_seen = true;
[188](#188)
[189](#189)        if acc != 0 {
[191](#191)            exponent = exponent
[192](#192)                .checked_mul(10)
[193](#193)                .and_then(|v| v.checked_add(digit as isize))
[194](#194)                .ok_or(INEXACT)?;
[195](#195)        }
[196](#196)    }
[197](#197)    if negative_exponent {
[198](#198)        exponent = -exponent;
[199](#199)    }
[200](#200)
[201](#201)    if acc == 0 {
[202](#202)        Ok((negative, 0, 0))
[204](#204)    } else {
[205](#205)        let exponent = nfracs
[209](#209)            .checked_mul(4)
[210](#210)            .and_then(|v| exponent.checked_sub(v))
[211](#211)            .ok_or(INEXACT)?;
[212](#212)        Ok((negative, acc, exponent))
[213](#213)    }
[214](#214)}
[215](#215)
[216](#216)#[test]
[217](#217)fn test_parse() {
[218](#218)    assert_eq!(parse(b"", false), Err(EMPTY));
[219](#219)    assert_eq!(parse(b" ", false), Err(INVALID));
[220](#220)    assert_eq!(parse(b"3.14", false), Err(INVALID));
[221](#221)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x3.14", false), Err(INVALID));
[222](#222)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x3.14fp+3", false), Ok((false, 0x314f, 3 - 12)));
[223](#223)    assert_eq!(parse(b" 0x3.14p+3", false), Err(INVALID));
[224](#224)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x3.14p+3 ", false), Err(INVALID));
[225](#225)    assert_eq!(parse(b"+0x3.14fp+3", false), Ok((false, 0x314f, 3 - 12)));
[226](#226)    assert_eq!(parse(b"-0x3.14fp+3", false), Ok((true, 0x314f, 3 - 12)));
[227](#227)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0xAbC.p1", false), Ok((false, 0xabc, 1)));
[228](#228)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0.7p1", false), Ok((false, 0x7, 1 - 4)));
[229](#229)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x.dEfP-1", false), Ok((false, 0xdef, -1 - 12)));
[230](#230)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x.p1", false), Err(INVALID));
[231](#231)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x.P1", false), Err(INVALID));
[232](#232)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0xp1", false), Err(INVALID));
[233](#233)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0xP1", false), Err(INVALID));
[234](#234)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0p", false), Err(INVALID));
[235](#235)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0xp", false), Err(INVALID));
[236](#236)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x.p", false), Err(INVALID));
[237](#237)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0p1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[238](#238)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0P1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[239](#239)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0.p1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[240](#240)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0.P1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[241](#241)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0.0p1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[242](#242)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0.0P1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[243](#243)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x.0p1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[244](#244)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x.0P1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[245](#245)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0p0", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[246](#246)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0.p999999999", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[247](#247)    assert_eq!(
[248](#248)        parse(b"0x0.p99999999999999999999999999999", false),
[249](#249)        Ok((false, 0, 0))
[250](#250)    );
[251](#251)    assert_eq!(
[252](#252)        parse(b"0x0.p-99999999999999999999999999999", false),
[253](#253)        Ok((false, 0, 0))
[254](#254)    );
[255](#255)    assert_eq!(
[256](#256)        parse(b"0x1.p99999999999999999999999999999", false),
[257](#257)        Err(INEXACT)
[258](#258)    );
[259](#259)    assert_eq!(
[260](#260)        parse(b"0x1.p-99999999999999999999999999999", false),
[261](#261)        Err(INEXACT)
[262](#262)    );
[263](#263)    assert_eq!(
[264](#264)        parse(b"0x4.00000000000000000000p55", false),
[265](#265)        Ok((false, 4, 55))
[266](#266)    );
[267](#267)    assert_eq!(
[268](#268)        parse(b"0x4.00001000000000000000p55", false),
[269](#269)        Ok((false, 0x400001, 55 - 20))
[270](#270)    );
[271](#271)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x4.00000000000000000001p55", false), Err(INEXACT));
[272](#272)
[273](#273)    assert_eq!(
[275](#275)        parse(b"-0x3____.1_4___p+___5___", true),
[276](#276)        Ok((true, 0x314, 5 - 8))
[277](#277)    );
[278](#278)    assert_eq!(parse(b"-_0x3.14p+5", true), Err(INVALID));
[279](#279)    assert_eq!(parse(b"_0x3.14p+5", true), Err(INVALID));
[280](#280)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x_3.14p+5", true), Err(INVALID));
[281](#281)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x3._14p+5", true), Err(INVALID));
[282](#282)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x3.14p_+5", true), Err(INVALID));
[283](#283)    assert_eq!(parse(b"-0x____.1_4___p+___5___", true), Err(INVALID));
[284](#284)    assert_eq!(parse(b"-0x3____.____p+___5___", true), Err(INVALID));
[285](#285)    assert_eq!(parse(b"-0x3____.1_4___p+______", true), Err(INVALID));
[286](#286)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x_p0", false), Err(INVALID));
[287](#287)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x_0p0", true), Err(INVALID));
[288](#288)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x_p0", true), Err(INVALID));
[289](#289)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x._p0", true), Err(INVALID));
[290](#290)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x._0p0", true), Err(INVALID));
[291](#291)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0._0p0", true), Err(INVALID));
[292](#292)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0_p0", true), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[293](#293)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x.0_p0", true), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[294](#294)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0.0_p0", true), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[295](#295)
[296](#296)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x1p-149", false), parse(b"0x1.0p-149", false));
[299](#299)}
[300](#300)
[301](#301)macro_rules! define_convert {
[302](#302)    ($name:ident => $f:ident) => {
[303](#303)        fn $name(negative: bool, mantissa: u64, exponent: isize) -> Result<$f, ParseHexfError> {
[304](#304)            if exponent < -0xffff || exponent > 0xffff {
[306](#306)                return Err(INEXACT);
[307](#307)            }
[308](#308)
[309](#309)            let trailing = mantissa.trailing_zeros() & 63; let mantissa = mantissa >> trailing;
[314](#314)            let exponent = exponent + trailing as isize;
[315](#315)
[316](#316)            let leading = mantissa.leading_zeros();
[319](#319)            let normalexp = exponent + (63 - leading as isize);
[320](#320)            let mantissasize = if normalexp < $f::MIN_EXP as isize - $f::MANTISSA_DIGITS as isize {
[321](#321)                return Err(INEXACT);
[323](#323)            } else if normalexp < ($f::MIN_EXP - 1) as isize {
[324](#324)                $f::MANTISSA_DIGITS as isize - $f::MIN_EXP as isize + normalexp + 1
[328](#328)            } else if normalexp < $f::MAX_EXP as isize {
[329](#329)                $f::MANTISSA_DIGITS as isize
[331](#331)            } else {
[332](#332)                return Err(INEXACT);
[335](#335)            };
[336](#336)
[337](#337)            if mantissa >> mantissasize == 0 {
[338](#338)                let mut mantissa = mantissa as $f;
[339](#339)                if negative {
[340](#340)                    mantissa = -mantissa;
[341](#341)                }
[342](#342)                Ok(mantissa * (2.0 as $f).powf(exponent as $f))
[344](#344)            } else {
[345](#345)                Err(INEXACT)
[346](#346)            }
[347](#347)        }
[348](#348)    };
[349](#349)}
[350](#350)
[351](#351)define_convert!(convert_hexf32 => f32);
[352](#352)define_convert!(convert_hexf64 => f64);
[353](#353)
[354](#354)#[test]
[355](#355)fn test_convert_hexf32() {
[356](#356)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf32(false, 0, 0), Ok(0.0));
[357](#357)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf32(false, 1, 0), Ok(1.0));
[358](#358)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf32(false, 10, 0), Ok(10.0));
[359](#359)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf32(false, 10, 1), Ok(20.0));
[360](#360)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf32(false, 10, -1), Ok(5.0));
[361](#361)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf32(true, 0, 0), Ok(-0.0));
[362](#362)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf32(true, 1, 0), Ok(-1.0));
[363](#363)
[364](#364)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf32(false, 0, 0).unwrap().signum(), 1.0);
[366](#366)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf32(true, 0, 0).unwrap().signum(), -1.0);
[367](#367)
[368](#368)    assert_eq!(
[370](#370)        convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_00ff_ffff, 0),
[371](#371)        Ok(16777215.0)
[372](#372)    );
[373](#373)    assert_eq!(
[374](#374)        convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_01ff_ffff, 0),
[375](#375)        Err(INEXACT)
[376](#376)    );
[377](#377)    assert_eq!(
[378](#378)        convert_hexf32(false, 0xffff_ff00_0000_0000, -40),
[379](#379)        Ok(16777215.0)
[380](#380)    );
[381](#381)    assert_eq!(
[382](#382)        convert_hexf32(false, 0xffff_ff80_0000_0000, -40),
[383](#383)        Err(INEXACT)
[384](#384)    );
[385](#385)
[386](#386)    assert!(convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_007f_ffff, -149).is_ok());
[388](#388)    assert!(convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_00ff_ffff, -150).is_err());
[389](#389)    assert!(convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_00ff_fffe, -150).is_ok());
[390](#390)    assert!(convert_hexf32(false, 0xffff_ff00_0000_0000, -190).is_err());
[391](#391)    assert!(convert_hexf32(false, 0xffff_fe00_0000_0000, -190).is_ok());
[392](#392)
[393](#393)    assert!(convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_0000_0001, -149).is_ok());
[395](#395)    assert!(convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_0000_0001, -150).is_err());
[396](#396)    assert!(convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_0000_0002, -150).is_ok());
[397](#397)    assert!(convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_0000_0002, -151).is_err());
[398](#398)    assert!(convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_0000_0003, -150).is_err());
[399](#399)    assert!(convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_0000_0003, -151).is_err());
[400](#400)    assert!(convert_hexf32(false, 0x8000_0000_0000_0000, -212).is_ok());
[401](#401)    assert!(convert_hexf32(false, 0x8000_0000_0000_0000, -213).is_err());
[402](#402)
[403](#403)    assert_eq!(
[405](#405)        convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_00ff_ffff, 104),
[406](#406)        Ok(f32::MAX)
[407](#407)    );
[408](#408)    assert_eq!(
[409](#409)        convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_01ff_ffff, 104),
[410](#410)        Err(INEXACT)
[411](#411)    );
[412](#412)    assert_eq!(
[413](#413)        convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_01ff_fffe, 104),
[414](#414)        Err(INEXACT)
[415](#415)    );
[416](#416)    assert_eq!(
[417](#417)        convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_0000_0001, 128),
[418](#418)        Err(INEXACT)
[419](#419)    );
[420](#420)    assert_eq!(
[421](#421)        convert_hexf32(false, 0x8000_0000_0000_0000, 65),
[422](#422)        Err(INEXACT)
[423](#423)    );
[424](#424)    assert_eq!(
[425](#425)        convert_hexf32(false, 0xffff_ff00_0000_0000, 64),
[426](#426)        Ok(f32::MAX)
[427](#427)    );
[428](#428)    assert_eq!(
[429](#429)        convert_hexf32(false, 0xffff_ff80_0000_0000, 64),
[430](#430)        Err(INEXACT)
[431](#431)    );
[432](#432)}

[435](#435)fn test_convert_hexf64() {
[436](#436)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf64(false, 0, 0), Ok(0.0));
[437](#437)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf64(false, 1, 0), Ok(1.0));
[438](#438)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf64(false, 10, 0), Ok(10.0));
[439](#439)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf64(false, 10, 1), Ok(20.0));

[441](#441)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf64(true, 0, 0), Ok(-0.0));
[442](#442)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf64(true, 1, 0), Ok(-1.0));
[443](#443)
[444](#444)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf64(false, 0, 0).unwrap().signum(), 1.0);
[446](#446)    assert_eq!(convert_hexf64(true, 0, 0).unwrap().signum(), -1.0);
[447](#447)
[448](#448)    assert_eq!(
[450](#450)        convert_hexf64(false, 0x001f_ffff_ffff_ffff, 0),

[479](#479)    assert!(convert_hexf64(false, 0x0000_0000_0000_0003, -1076).is_err());
[480](#480)    assert!(convert_hexf64(false, 0x8000_0000_0000_0000, -1137).is_ok());
[481](#481)    assert!(convert_hexf64(false, 0x8000_0000_0000_0000, -1138).is_err());
[482](#482)
[483](#483)    assert_eq!(
[485](#485)        convert_hexf64(false, 0x001f_ffff_ffff_ffff, 971),
[486](#486)        Ok(f64::MAX)
[487](#487)    );
[488](#488)    assert_eq!(
[489](#489)        convert_hexf64(false, 0x003f_ffff_ffff_ffff, 971),
[490](#490)        Err(INEXACT)
[491](#491)    );
[492](#492)    assert_eq!(
[493](#493)        convert_hexf64(false, 0x003f_ffff_ffff_fffe, 971),
[494](#494)        Err(INEXACT)
[495](#495)    );
[496](#496)    assert_eq!(
[497](#497)        convert_hexf32(false, 0x0000_0000_0000_0001, 1024),
[498](#498)        Err(INEXACT)
[499](#499)    );
[500](#500)    assert_eq!(
[501](#501)        convert_hexf32(false, 0x8000_0000_0000_0000, 961),
[502](#502)        Err(INEXACT)
[503](#503)    );
[504](#504)    assert_eq!(

# hexf_parse - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/hexf-parse/latest/hexf_parse/

## Expand description

Parses hexadecimal float literals.
There are two functions `parse_hexf32` and `parse_hexf64` provided for each type.

```
use hexf_parse::*;
assert_eq!(parse_hexf32("0x1.99999ap-4", false), Ok(0.1f32));
assert_eq!(parse_hexf64("0x1.999999999999ap-4", false), Ok(0.1f64));
```
An additional `bool` parameter can be set to true if you want to allow underscores.

```
use hexf_parse::*;
assert!(parse_hexf64("0x0.1_7p8", false).is_err());
assert_eq!(parse_hexf64("0x0.1_7p8", true), Ok(23.0f64));
```
The error is reported via an opaque `ParseHexfError` type.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseHexfError.html)- Hexf - Error
- An opaque error type from `parse_hexf32`and`parse_hexf64`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_hexf32.html)- hexf32
- Tries to parse a hexadecimal float literal to `f32`. The underscore is allowed only when`allow_underscore`is true.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_hexf64.html)- hexf64
- Tries to parse a hexadecimal float literal to `f64`. The underscore is allowed only when`allow_underscore`is true.

# hexf_parse - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/hexf-parse/latest/target-redirect/hexf_parse/index.html

## Expand description

Parses hexadecimal float literals.
There are two functions `parse_hexf32` and `parse_hexf64` provided for each type.

```
use hexf_parse::*;
assert_eq!(parse_hexf32("0x1.99999ap-4", false), Ok(0.1f32));
assert_eq!(parse_hexf64("0x1.999999999999ap-4", false), Ok(0.1f64));
```
An additional `bool` parameter can be set to true if you want to allow underscores.

```
use hexf_parse::*;
assert!(parse_hexf64("0x0.1_7p8", false).is_err());
assert_eq!(parse_hexf64("0x0.1_7p8", true), Ok(23.0f64));
```
The error is reported via an opaque `ParseHexfError` type.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseHexfError.html)- Hexf - Error
- An opaque error type from `parse_hexf32`and`parse_hexf64`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- Tries to parse a hexadecimal float literal to `f32`. The underscore is allowed only when`allow_underscore`is true.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_hexf64.html)- hexf64

[67](#67)fn parse(s: &[u8], allow_underscore: bool) -> Result<(bool, u64, isize), ParseHexfError> {
[68](#68)    let (s, negative) = match s.split_first() {
[70](#70)        Some((&b'+', s)) => (s, false),
[71](#71)        Some((&b'-', s)) => (s, true),
[72](#72)        Some(_) => (s, false),
[73](#73)        None => return Err(EMPTY),
[74](#74)    };
[75](#75)
[76](#76)    if !(s.starts_with(b"0x") || s.starts_with(b"0X")) {
[78](#78)        return Err(INVALID);
[79](#79)    }
[80](#80)
[81](#81)    let mut s = &s[2..];
[83](#83)    let mut acc = 0; let mut digit_seen = false;
[85](#85)    loop {
[86](#86)        let (s_, digit) = match s.split_first() {
[87](#87)            Some((&c @ b'0'..=b'9', s)) => (s, c - b'0'),
[88](#88)            Some((&c @ b'a'..=b'f', s)) => (s, c - b'a' + 10),
[89](#89)            Some((&c @ b'A'..=b'F', s)) => (s, c - b'A' + 10),
[90](#90)            Some((&b'_', s_)) if allow_underscore && digit_seen => {
[91](#91)                s = s_;
[92](#92)                continue;
[93](#93)            }
[94](#94)            _ => break,
[95](#95)        };
[96](#96)
[97](#97)        s = s_;
[98](#98)        digit_seen = true;
[99](#99)
[100](#100)        if acc >> 60 != 0 {
[102](#102)            return Err(INEXACT);
[103](#103)        }
[104](#104)        acc = acc << 4 | digit as u64;
[105](#105)    }
[106](#106)
[107](#107)    let mut nfracs = 0isize; let mut nzeroes = 0isize;
[112](#112)    let mut frac_digit_seen = false;
[113](#113)    if s.starts_with(b".") {
[114](#114)        s = &s[1..];
[115](#115)        loop {
[116](#116)            let (s_, digit) = match s.split_first() {
[117](#117)                Some((&c @ b'0'..=b'9', s)) => (s, c - b'0'),
[118](#118)                Some((&c @ b'a'..=b'f', s)) => (s, c - b'a' + 10),
[119](#119)                Some((&c @ b'A'..=b'F', s)) => (s, c - b'A' + 10),
[120](#120)                Some((&b'_', s_)) if allow_underscore && frac_digit_seen => {
[121](#121)                    s = s_;
[122](#122)                    continue;
[123](#123)                }
[124](#124)                _ => break,
[125](#125)            };
[126](#126)
[127](#127)            s = s_;
[128](#128)            frac_digit_seen = true;
[129](#129)
[130](#130)            if digit == 0 {
[131](#131)                nzeroes = nzeroes.checked_add(1).ok_or(INEXACT)?;
[132](#132)            } else {
[133](#133)                let nnewdigits = nzeroes.checked_add(1).ok_or(INEXACT)?;
[135](#135)                nfracs = nfracs.checked_add(nnewdigits).ok_or(INEXACT)?;
[136](#136)                nzeroes = 0;
[137](#137)
[138](#138)                if acc != 0 {
[142](#142)                    if nnewdigits >= 16 || acc >> (64 - nnewdigits * 4) != 0 {
[143](#143)                        return Err(INEXACT);
[144](#144)                    }
[145](#145)                    acc = acc << (nnewdigits * 4);
[146](#146)                }
[147](#147)                acc |= digit as u64;
[148](#148)            }
[149](#149)        }
[150](#150)    }
[151](#151)
[152](#152)    if !(digit_seen || frac_digit_seen) {
[154](#154)        return Err(INVALID);
[155](#155)    }
[156](#156)
[157](#157)    let s = match s.split_first() {
[159](#159)        Some((&b'P', s)) | Some((&b'p', s)) => s,
[160](#160)        _ => return Err(INVALID),
[161](#161)    };
[162](#162)
[163](#163)    let (mut s, negative_exponent) = match s.split_first() {
[165](#165)        Some((&b'+', s)) => (s, false),
[166](#166)        Some((&b'-', s)) => (s, true),
[167](#167)        Some(_) => (s, false),
[168](#168)        None => return Err(INVALID),
[169](#169)    };
[170](#170)
[171](#171)    let mut digit_seen = false;
[173](#173)    let mut exponent = 0isize; loop {
[175](#175)        let (s_, digit) = match s.split_first() {
[176](#176)            Some((&c @ b'0'..=b'9', s)) => (s, c - b'0'),
[177](#177)            Some((&b'_', s_)) if allow_underscore => {
[178](#178)                s = s_;
[179](#179)                continue;
[180](#180)            }
[181](#181)            None if digit_seen => break,
[182](#182)            _ => return Err(INVALID),
[184](#184)        };
[185](#185)
[186](#186)        s = s_;
[187](#187)        digit_seen = true;
[188](#188)
[189](#189)        if acc != 0 {
[191](#191)            exponent = exponent
[192](#192)                .checked_mul(10)
[193](#193)                .and_then(|v| v.checked_add(digit as isize))
[194](#194)                .ok_or(INEXACT)?;
[195](#195)        }
[196](#196)    }
[197](#197)    if negative_exponent {
[198](#198)        exponent = -exponent;
[199](#199)    }
[200](#200)
[201](#201)    if acc == 0 {
[202](#202)        Ok((negative, 0, 0))
[204](#204)    } else {
[205](#205)        let exponent = nfracs
[209](#209)            .checked_mul(4)
[210](#210)            .and_then(|v| exponent.checked_sub(v))
[211](#211)            .ok_or(INEXACT)?;
[212](#212)        Ok((negative, acc, exponent))
[213](#213)    }
[214](#214)}
[215](#215)
[216](#216)#[test]
[217](#217)fn test_parse() {
[218](#218)    assert_eq!(parse(b"", false), Err(EMPTY));
[219](#219)    assert_eq!(parse(b" ", false), Err(INVALID));
[220](#220)    assert_eq!(parse(b"3.14", false), Err(INVALID));
[221](#221)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x3.14", false), Err(INVALID));
[222](#222)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x3.14fp+3", false), Ok((false, 0x314f, 3 - 12)));
[223](#223)    assert_eq!(parse(b" 0x3.14p+3", false), Err(INVALID));
[224](#224)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x3.14p+3 ", false), Err(INVALID));
[225](#225)    assert_eq!(parse(b"+0x3.14fp+3", false), Ok((false, 0x314f, 3 - 12)));
[226](#226)    assert_eq!(parse(b"-0x3.14fp+3", false), Ok((true, 0x314f, 3 - 12)));
[227](#227)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0xAbC.p1", false), Ok((false, 0xabc, 1)));
[228](#228)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0.7p1", false), Ok((false, 0x7, 1 - 4)));
[229](#229)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x.dEfP-1", false), Ok((false, 0xdef, -1 - 12)));
[230](#230)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x.p1", false), Err(INVALID));
[231](#231)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x.P1", false), Err(INVALID));
[232](#232)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0xp1", false), Err(INVALID));
[233](#233)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0xP1", false), Err(INVALID));
[234](#234)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0p", false), Err(INVALID));
[235](#235)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0xp", false), Err(INVALID));
[236](#236)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x.p", false), Err(INVALID));
[237](#237)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0p1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[238](#238)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0P1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[239](#239)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0.p1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[240](#240)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0.P1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[241](#241)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0.0p1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[242](#242)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0.0P1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[243](#243)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x.0p1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[244](#244)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x.0P1", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[245](#245)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0p0", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[246](#246)    assert_eq!(parse(b"0x0.p999999999", false), Ok((false, 0, 0)));
[247](#247)    assert_eq!(
[248](#248)        parse(b"0x0.p99999999999999999999999999999", false),

[300](#300)
[301](#301)macro_rules! define_convert {
[302](#302)    ($name:ident => $f:ident) => {
[303](#303)        fn $name(negative: bool, mantissa: u64, exponent: isize) -> Result<$f, ParseHexfError> {
[304](#304)            if exponent < -0xffff || exponent > 0xffff {
[306](#306)                return Err(INEXACT);
[307](#307)            }
[308](#308)
[309](#309)            let trailing = mantissa.trailing_zeros() & 63; let mantissa = mantissa >> trailing;
[314](#314)            let exponent = exponent + trailing as isize;
[315](#315)
[316](#316)            let leading = mantissa.leading_zeros();
[319](#319)            let normalexp = exponent + (63 - leading as isize);
[320](#320)            let mantissasize = if normalexp < $f::MIN_EXP as isize - $f::MANTISSA_DIGITS as isize {
[321](#321)                return Err(INEXACT);
[323](#323)            } else if normalexp < ($f::MIN_EXP - 1) as isize {
[324](#324)                $f::MANTISSA_DIGITS as isize - $f::MIN_EXP as isize + normalexp + 1
[328](#328)            } else if normalexp < $f::MAX_EXP as isize {
[329](#329)                $f::MANTISSA_DIGITS as isize
[331](#331)            } else {
[332](#332)                return Err(INEXACT);
[335](#335)            };
[336](#336)
[337](#337)            if mantissa >> mantissasize == 0 {
[338](#338)                let mut mantissa = mantissa as $f;
[339](#339)                if negative {
[340](#340)                    mantissa = -mantissa;
[341](#341)                }
[342](#342)                Ok(mantissa * (2.0 as $f).powf(exponent as $f))
[344](#344)            } else {
[345](#345)                Err(INEXACT)
[346](#346)            }
[347](#347)        }
[348](#348)    };
[349](#349)}

[352](#352)define_convert!(convert_hexf64 => f64);

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap::Command

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
