# tracing_opentelemetry - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tracing-opentelemetry/^0.33/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#tracing-opentelemetry)Tracing OpenTelemetry

[ tracing](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tracing) is a framework for instrumenting Rust programs to collect
structured, event-based diagnostic information. This crate provides a layer
that connects spans from multiple systems into a trace and emits them to

[OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io)-compatible distributed tracing systems for processing and visualization.

[§](https://docs.rs#special-fields)Special Fields

Fields with an `otel.` prefix are reserved for this crate and have specific
meaning. They are treated as ordinary fields by other layers. The current
special fields are:

- `otel.name`: Override the span name sent to OpenTelemetry exporters. Setting this field is useful if you want to display non-static information in your span name.
- `otel.kind`: Set the span kind to one of the supported OpenTelemetry- [span kinds](https://docs.rs/opentelemetry/0.32.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/opentelemetry/trace/span/enum.SpanKind.html). These must be specified as strings such as- `"client"`or- `"server"`. If it is not specified, the span is assumed to be internal.
- `otel.status_code`: Set the span status code to one of the supported OpenTelemetry- [span status codes](https://docs.rs/opentelemetry/0.32.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/opentelemetry/trace/span/enum.Status.html).
- `otel.status_description`: Set the span description of the status. This should be used only if- `otel.status_code`is also set.

[§](https://docs.rs#semantic-conventions)Semantic Conventions

OpenTelemetry defines conventional names for attributes of common
operations. These names can be assigned directly as fields, e.g.
`trace_span!("request", "server.port" = 80, "url.full" = ..)`, and they
will be passed through to your configured OpenTelemetry exporter. You can
find the full list of the operations and their expected field names in the
[semantic conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions) spec.

[§](https://docs.rs#stability-status)Stability Status

The OpenTelemetry tracing specification is stable but the underlying [opentelemetry crate](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-rust) is
not so some breaking changes will still occur in this crate as well. Metrics are not yet fully
stable. You can read the specification via the [spec repository](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification).

[§](https://docs.rs#opentelemetry-logging)OpenTelemetry Logging

Logging to OpenTelemetry collectors is not supported by this crate, only traces and metrics are.
If you need to export logs through OpenTelemetry, consider [ opentelemetry-appender-tracing](https://crates.io/crates/opentelemetry-appender-tracing).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use opentelemetry_sdk::trace::SdkTracerProvider;
use opentelemetry::trace::{Tracer, TracerProvider as _};
use tracing::{error, span};
use tracing_subscriber::layer::SubscriberExt;
use tracing_subscriber::Registry;
// Create a new OpenTelemetry trace pipeline that prints to stdout
let provider = SdkTracerProvider::builder()
    .with_simple_exporter(opentelemetry_stdout::SpanExporter::default())
    .build();
let tracer = provider.tracer("readme_example");
// Create a tracing layer with the configured tracer
let telemetry = tracing_opentelemetry::layer().with_tracer(tracer);
// Use the tracing subscriber `Registry`, or any other subscriber
// that impls `LookupSpan`
let subscriber = Registry::default().with(telemetry);
// Trace executed code
tracing::subscriber::with_default(subscriber, || {
    // Spans will be sent to the configured OpenTelemetry exporter
    let root = span!(tracing::Level::TRACE, "app_start", work_units = 2);
    let _enter = root.enter();
    error!("This event will be logged in the root span.");
});
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

- `metrics`: Enables the- `MetricsLayer`- [layer](https://docs.rs/tracing-subscriber/0.3.23/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing_subscriber/layer/index.html)that exports OpenTelemetry metrics from specifically-named events. This enables the- `metrics`feature flag on the- `opentelemetry`crate.- *Enabled by default*.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Filtered](https://docs.rs/struct.FilteredOpenTelemetryLayer.html)- Open - Telemetry - Layer
- A layer wrapping a `OpenTelemetryLayer``Filter``OpenTelemetryLayer::with_counting_event_filter`
- [Metrics](https://docs.rs/struct.MetricsLayer.html)- Layer - `metrics`
- A layer that publishes metrics via the OpenTelemetry SDK.
- [Open](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenTelemetryLayer.html)- Telemetry - Layer
- An [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io)propagation layer for use in a project that uses[tracing](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tracing).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [SetParent](https://docs.rs/enum.SetParentError.html)- Error
- An error returned if `OpenTelemetrySpanExt::set_parent`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Open](https://docs.rs/trait.OpenTelemetrySpanExt.html)- Telemetry - Span - Ext
- Utility functions to allow tracing `Span`[OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io)`Context`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_otel_context.html)- otel_ - context
- Utility functions to allow `tracing::span::Id`[OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io)`Context``Extensions``ExtensionsMut`
- [layer](https://docs.rs/fn.layer.html)
- Construct a layer to track spans via [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io).

# tracing_subscriber - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tracing-subscriber/^0.3/

## Expand description

Utilities for implementing and composing [ tracing](https://docs.rs/tracing/latest/tracing) subscribers.

[ tracing](https://docs.rs/tracing/latest/tracing) is a framework for instrumenting Rust programs to collect
scoped, structured, and async-aware diagnostics. The

[trait represents the functionality necessary to collect this trace data. This crate contains tools for composing subscribers out of smaller units of behaviour, and batteries-included implementations of common subscriber functionality.](https://docs.rs/tracing-core/0.1.35/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing_core/subscriber/trait.Subscriber.html)

`Subscriber``tracing-subscriber` is intended for use by both `Subscriber` authors and
application authors using `tracing` to instrument their applications.

*Compiler support:  requires *

`rustc` 1.65+[§](https://docs.rs#layers-and-filters)`Layer`s and `Filter`s

The most important component of the `tracing-subscriber` API is the
[ Layer](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Layer.html) trait, which provides a composable abstraction for building

[s. Like the](https://docs.rs/tracing-core/0.1.35/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing_core/subscriber/trait.Subscriber.html)

`Subscriber`[trait, a](https://docs.rs/tracing-core/0.1.35/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing_core/subscriber/trait.Subscriber.html)

`Subscriber`[defines a particular behavior for collecting trace data. Unlike](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`[s, which implement a](https://docs.rs/tracing-core/0.1.35/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing_core/subscriber/trait.Subscriber.html)

`Subscriber`*complete*strategy for how trace data is collected,

[s provide](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`*modular*implementations of specific behaviors. Therefore, they can be

[composed together](https://docs.rs/layer/index.html#composing-layers)to form a

[which is capable of recording traces in a variety of ways. See the](https://docs.rs/tracing-core/0.1.35/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing_core/subscriber/trait.Subscriber.html)

`Subscriber`[for details on using](https://docs.rs/layer/index.html)

`layer` module’s
documentation[s.](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`In addition, the [ Filter](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Filter.html) trait defines an interface for filtering what
spans and events are recorded by a particular layer. This allows different

[s to handle separate subsets of the trace data emitted by a program. See the](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`[documentation on per-layer filtering](https://docs.rs/layer/index.html#per-layer-filtering)for more information on using

[s.](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Filter.html)

`Filter`[§](https://docs.rs#included-subscribers)Included Subscribers

The following `Subscriber`s are provided for application authors:

- `fmt`- `fmt`feature flag)

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

- `std`: Enables APIs that depend on the Rust standard library (enabled by default).
- `alloc`: Depend on- `liballoc`
- `env-filter`: Enables the- `EnvFilter`- `env_logger`crate- **Requires “std”**.
- `fmt`: Enables the- `fmt`- **Requires “registry” and “std”**.
- `ansi`: Enables- `fmt`support for ANSI terminal colors. Enabled by default.
- `registry`: enables the- `registry`- **Requires “std”**.
- `json`: Enables- `fmt`support for JSON output. In JSON output, the ANSI feature does nothing.- **Requires “fmt” and “std”**.
- `local-time`: Enables local time formatting when using the- `time`crate- `fmt`subscriber.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-dependencies)Optional Dependencies

- `tracing-log`- `log`macros in the- `fmt`subscriber. Enabled by default.
- `time`- `time`crate- `fmt`subscriber.
- `smallvec`- `EnvFilter`type to use the- `smallvec`crate (rather than- `Vec`) as a performance optimization. Enabled by default.
- `parking_lot`- `parking_lot`crate’s- `RwLock`implementation rather than the Rust standard library’s implementation.

[§](https://docs.rs#no_std-support)`no_std` Support

In embedded systems and other bare-metal applications, `tracing` can be
used without requiring the Rust standard library, although some features are
disabled. Although most of the APIs provided by `tracing-subscriber`, such
as [ fmt](https://docs.rs/fmt/index.html) and

[, require the standard library, some functionality, such as the](https://docs.rs/filter/struct.EnvFilter.html)

`EnvFilter`[trait, can still be used in](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer``no_std` environments.The dependency on the standard library is controlled by two crate feature
flags, “std”, which enables the dependency on [ libstd](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/index.html), and “alloc”, which
enables the dependency on

[(and is enabled by the “std” feature). These features are enabled by default, but](https://doc.rust-lang.org/alloc/index.html)

`liballoc``no_std` users can
disable them using:```
# Cargo.toml
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", default-features = false }
```
Additional APIs are available when [ liballoc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/alloc/index.html) is available. To enable

`liballoc` but not `std`, use:```
# Cargo.toml
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", default-features = false, features = ["alloc"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-features)Unstable Features

These feature flags enable **unstable** features. The public API may break in 0.1.x
releases. To enable these features, the `--cfg tracing_unstable` must be passed to
`rustc` when compiling.

The following unstable feature flags are currently available:

- `valuable`: Enables support for serializing values recorded using the- `valuable`- `format::Json`

[§](https://docs.rs#enabling-unstable-features)Enabling Unstable Features

The easiest way to set the `tracing_unstable` cfg is to use the `RUSTFLAGS`
env variable when running `cargo` commands:

`RUSTFLAGS="--cfg tracing_unstable" cargo build`Alternatively, the following can be added to the `.cargo/config` file in a
project to automatically enable the cfg flag for that project:

```
[build]
rustflags = ["--cfg", "tracing_unstable"]
```
[§](https://docs.rs#supported-rust-versions)Supported Rust Versions

Tracing is built against the latest stable release. The minimum supported version is 1.65. The current Tracing version is not guaranteed to build on Rust versions earlier than the minimum supported version.

Tracing follows the same compiler support policies as the rest of the Tokio project. The current stable Rust compiler and the three most recent minor versions before it will always be supported. For example, if the current stable compiler version is 1.69, the minimum supported version will not be increased past 1.66, three minor versions prior. Increasing the minimum supported compiler version is not considered a semver breaking change as long as doing so complies with this policy.

# url - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/url/^2/

## Expand description

rust-url is an implementation of the [URL Standard](http://url.spec.whatwg.org/)
for the [Rust](http://rust-lang.org/) programming language.

[§](https://docs.rs#url-parsing-and-data-structures)URL parsing and data structures

First, URL parsing may fail for various reasons and therefore returns a `Result`.

```
use url::{Url, ParseError};
assert!(Url::parse("http://[:::1]") == Err(ParseError::InvalidIpv6Address))
```
Let’s parse a valid URL and look at its components.

```
use url::{Url, Host, Position};
let issue_list_url = Url::parse(
    "https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues?labels=E-easy&state=open"
)?;
assert!(issue_list_url.scheme() == "https");
assert!(issue_list_url.username() == "");
assert!(issue_list_url.password() == None);
assert!(issue_list_url.host_str() == Some("github.com"));
assert!(issue_list_url.host() == Some(Host::Domain("github.com")));
assert!(issue_list_url.port() == None);
assert!(issue_list_url.path() == "/rust-lang/rust/issues");
assert!(issue_list_url.path_segments().map(|c| c.collect::<Vec<_>>()) ==
        Some(vec!["rust-lang", "rust", "issues"]));
assert!(issue_list_url.query() == Some("labels=E-easy&state=open"));
assert!(&issue_list_url[Position::BeforePath..] == "/rust-lang/rust/issues?labels=E-easy&state=open");
assert!(issue_list_url.fragment() == None);
assert!(!issue_list_url.cannot_be_a_base());
```
Some URLs are said to be *cannot-be-a-base*:
they don’t have a username, password, host, or port,
and their “path” is an arbitrary string rather than slash-separated segments:

```
use url::Url;
let data_url = Url::parse("data:text/plain,Hello?World#")?;
assert!(data_url.cannot_be_a_base());
assert!(data_url.scheme() == "data");
assert!(data_url.path() == "text/plain,Hello");
assert!(data_url.path_segments().is_none());
assert!(data_url.query() == Some("World"));
assert!(data_url.fragment() == Some(""));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#default-features)Default Features

Versions `<= 2.5.2` of the crate have no default features. Versions `> 2.5.2` have the default feature ‘std’.
If you are upgrading across this boundary and you have specified `default-features = false`, then
you will need to add the ‘std’ feature or the ‘alloc’ feature to your dependency.
The ‘std’ feature has the same behavior as the previous versions. The ‘alloc’ feature
provides no_std support.

[§](https://docs.rs#serde)Serde

Enable the `serde` feature to include `Deserialize` and `Serialize` implementations for `url::Url`.

[§](https://docs.rs#base-url)Base URL

Many contexts allow URL *references* that can be relative to a *base URL*:

`<link rel="stylesheet" href="../main.css">`Since parsed URLs are absolute, giving a base is required for parsing relative URLs:

```
use url::{Url, ParseError};
assert!(Url::parse("../main.css") == Err(ParseError::RelativeUrlWithoutBase))
```
Use the `join` method on an `Url` to use it as a base URL:

```
use url::Url;
let this_document = Url::parse("http://servo.github.io/rust-url/url/index.html")?;
let css_url = this_document.join("../main.css")?;
assert_eq!(css_url.as_str(), "http://servo.github.io/rust-url/main.css");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-serde)Feature: `serde`

If you enable the `serde` feature, [ Url](https://docs.rs/struct.Url.html) will implement

[and](https://docs.rs/serde/1/serde/trait.Serialize.html)

`serde::Serialize`[. See](https://docs.rs/serde/1/serde/trait.Deserialize.html)

`serde::Deserialize`[serde documentation](https://serde.rs)for more information.

`url = { version = "2", features = ["serde"] }`[§](https://docs.rs#feature-debugger_visualizer)Feature: `debugger_visualizer`

If you enable the `debugger_visualizer` feature, the `url` crate will include
a [natvis file](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/debugger/create-custom-views-of-native-objects)
for [Visual Studio](https://www.visualstudio.com/) that allows you to view
[ Url](https://docs.rs/struct.Url.html) objects in the debugger.

This feature requires Rust 1.71 or later.

`url = { version = "2", features = ["debugger_visualizer"] }`## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [form_urlencoded](https://docs.rs/form_urlencoded/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/form_urlencoded/index.html);

# futures_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/futures-util/^0.3/

## Expand description

Combinators and utilities for working with `Future`s, `Stream`s, `Sink`s,
and the `AsyncRead` and `AsyncWrite` traits.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [join](https://docs.rs/macro.join.html)- `async-await-macro`and- `async-await`
- Polls multiple futures simultaneously, returning a tuple of all results once complete.
- [pending](https://docs.rs/macro.pending.html)- `async-await`
- A macro which yields to the event loop once.
- [pin_mut](https://docs.rs/macro.pin_mut.html)
- Pins a value on the stack.
- [poll](https://docs.rs/macro.poll.html)- `async-await`
- A macro which returns the result of polling a future once within the
current `async`context.
- [ready](https://docs.rs/macro.ready.html)
- Extracts the successful type of `Poll<T>`.
- [select](https://docs.rs/macro.select.html)- `async-await-macro`and- `async-await`and- `std`
- Polls multiple futures and streams simultaneously, executing the branch
for the future that finishes first. If multiple futures are ready,
one will be pseudo-randomly selected at runtime. Futures directly
passed to `select!`must be`Unpin`and implement`FusedFuture`.
- [select_](https://docs.rs/macro.select_biased.html)- biased - `async-await-macro`and- `async-await`
- Polls multiple futures and streams simultaneously, executing the branch
for the future that finishes first. Unlike `select!``select_biased!`must be`Unpin`and implement`FusedFuture`.
- [stream_](https://docs.rs/macro.stream_select.html)- select - `async-await-macro`and- `async-await`and- `std`
- Combines several streams, all producing the same `Item`type, into one stream. This is similar to`select_all`but does not require the streams to all be the same type. It also keeps the streams inline, and does not require`Box<dyn Stream>`s to be allocated. Streams passed to this macro must be`Unpin`.
- [try_](https://docs.rs/macro.try_join.html)- join - `async-await-macro`and- `async-await`
- Polls multiple futures simultaneously, resolving to a `Result`

# smooth_operator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#smooth-operator)smooth-operator

The reference core for smooth-operator — the service layer on top of
[ smooth_operator_core](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/index.html) (the agent engine). It defines three things:

- `domain`- `spec/domain/*.json`. Checkpoints re-use the engine’s- `smooth_operator_core::Checkpoint`
- `adapter`- `StorageAdapter`- `docs/STORAGE.md`). Its checkpoint/knowledge accessors return smooth-operator-core’s own traits so the engine plugs straight in.
- `runtime`- `AgentRuntime`- `Agent`- `Workflow`

It also owns two shared retrieval seams both backends/consumers depend on:
[ embedding](https://docs.rs/embedding/index.html) (the text→vector

[+ the network-free](https://docs.rs/embedding/trait.Embedder.html)

`Embedder`[, the one home for both the Postgres adapter and the ingestion pipeline) and](https://docs.rs/embedding/struct.DeterministicEmbedder.html)

`DeterministicEmbedder`[(the optional post-retrieval](https://docs.rs/rerank/index.html)

`rerank`[stage — feature gap G8).](https://docs.rs/rerank/trait.Reranker.html)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [access_](https://docs.rs/access_control/index.html)- control
- Document-level access control (feature gap G3).
- [adapter](https://docs.rs/adapter/index.html)
- The `StorageAdapter`seam.
- [agent_](https://docs.rs/agent_config/index.html)- config
- Per-agent behavior config (SMOODEV-590 parity in Rust).
- [auth](https://docs.rs/auth/index.html)
- Authentication + role-based access control (Phase 12).
- [backplane](https://docs.rs/backplane/index.html)
- Connection backplane: the scale-out + event-delivery seam for the WebSocket server.
- [connector_](https://docs.rs/connector_config/index.html)- config
- Connector configuration storage (Phase 12, increment 3).
- [curation](https://docs.rs/curation/index.html)
- Document sets, curation boosting, and query-time metadata filters (feature gap, Phase 11 — “Document sets / curation / boosting”).
- [domain](https://docs.rs/domain/index.html)
- Domain model for smooth-operator.
- [embedding](https://docs.rs/embedding/index.html)
- Text → vector embedding — the shared seam for dense retrieval.
- [gateway_](https://docs.rs/gateway_key/index.html)- key
- Per-org LLM gateway-key resolution: the seam that lets a multi-tenant
deployment bill/scope each org’s turns to its **own**gateway key while a standalone/local server keeps using the single environment key.
- [otp](https://docs.rs/otp/index.html)
- End-user identity verification (OTP) — the seam that lets a host wire a
one-time-code flow behind a public agent’s `end_user`tool auth, while the reference server stays credential-free.
- [rerank](https://docs.rs/rerank/index.html)
- Reranking — the optional post-retrieval reorder stage (feature gap G8).
- [runtime](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html)
- Minimal `AgentRuntime`that proves smooth-operator consumes smooth-operator.
- [settings](https://docs.rs/settings/index.html)
- Per-org agent settings storage (Phase 12, increment 3).
- [telemetry](https://docs.rs/telemetry/index.html)
- OpenTelemetry GenAI instrumentation for the agent turn.
- [tool_](https://docs.rs/tool_provider/index.html)- provider
- Host-contributed tool injection seam.
- [tools](https://docs.rs/tools/index.html)
- Tools the smooth-operator runtime registers on the smooth-operator-core engine.
- [widget_](https://docs.rs/widget_auth/index.html)- auth
- Embeddable-widget auth: an origin allowlist + public-key `authContext`verification for browser-embedded chat widgets (`<smooth-agent-chat>`).

# smooth_operator_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#smooth-operator)Smooth Operator

An embeddable, polyglot AI agent engine with built-in checkpointing, tool system, and LLM client.

Inspired by LangGraph, CrewAI, and Agno — purpose-built for orchestrated agent workloads with security-first design.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [activities](https://docs.rs/activities/index.html)
- Deterministic turn orchestration over a pluggable I/O surface.
- [agent](https://docs.rs/agent/index.html)
- [cast](https://docs.rs/cast/index.html)
- Cast — operator roles
- [checkpoint](https://docs.rs/checkpoint/index.html)
- [context](https://docs.rs/context/index.html)
- Project context loader — parses AGENTS.md (or its fallbacks) and resolves file references.
- [conversation](https://docs.rs/conversation/index.html)
- [cost](https://docs.rs/cost/index.html)
- Cost tracking and budget enforcement for LLM usage.
- [executor](https://docs.rs/executor/index.html)
- Agent execution backend abstraction.
- [human](https://docs.rs/human/index.html)
- Human-in-the-loop support for agent tool execution.
- [knowledge](https://docs.rs/knowledge/index.html)
- [llm](https://docs.rs/llm/index.html)
- [llm_](https://docs.rs/llm_provider/index.html)- provider
- An `LlmProvider`seam over the LLM call so the agent loop and workflows can be unit-tested deterministically, without a live model or network.
- [memory](https://docs.rs/memory/index.html)
- [providers](https://docs.rs/providers/index.html)
- [quirks](https://docs.rs/quirks/index.html)
- Per-model wire-format quirks.
- [resolution](https://docs.rs/resolution/index.html)
- Alias resolution for LiteLLM-backed gateways.
- [tool](https://docs.rs/tool/index.html)
- [tool_](https://docs.rs/tool_search/index.html)- search
- `tool_search`meta-tool — promotes deferred tools on demand (pearl th-cfa1fb).
- [workflow](https://docs.rs/workflow/index.html)
- LangGraph-inspired typed workflow graph with conditional edges.
- [ws_](https://docs.rs/ws_resilience/index.html)- resilience
- WebSocket connection resiliency — shared logic for WebSocket-based agent clients.

# smooth_operator::domain - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/domain/index.html

## Expand description

Domain model for smooth-operator.

These structs mirror `spec/domain/*.json` exactly (field names, optionality)
and are storage-agnostic — no backend is named here. They are the shapes the
`StorageAdapter` (see [ crate::adapter](https://docs.rs/adapter/index.html)) reads and writes.

Checkpoints are *not* redefined here: we re-use smooth-operator’s
[ Checkpoint](https://docs.rs/struct.Checkpoint.html) directly so the engine plugs
straight into the checkpoint slice. See

[.](https://docs.rs/adapter/index.html)

`crate::adapter`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Checkpoint](https://docs.rs/struct.Checkpoint.html)
- A checkpoint captures the full state of an agent at a point in time.
- [Citation](https://docs.rs/struct.Citation.html)
- A source the agent used to ground its answer.
- [Content](https://docs.rs/struct.ContentItem.html)- Item
- A single content element within a message.
Mirrors `message.schema.json#/$defs/ContentItem`.
- [Conversation](https://docs.rs/struct.Conversation.html)
- A conversation thread between participants.
Mirrors `conversation.schema.json`.
- [Message](https://docs.rs/struct.Message.html)
- A single message within a conversation.
Mirrors `message.schema.json`.
- [Message](https://docs.rs/struct.MessageContent.html)- Content
- Structured content of a message.
Mirrors `message.schema.json#/$defs/MessageContent`.
- [Participant](https://docs.rs/struct.Participant.html)
- A participant in a conversation.
Mirrors `participant.schema.json`.
- [Participant](https://docs.rs/struct.ParticipantRef.html)- Ref
- Abbreviated sender/recipient descriptor (wire shape).
Mirrors `message.schema.json#/properties/from`(and`to`).
- [Session](https://docs.rs/struct.Session.html)
- An AI conversation session — ties a conversation to a smooth-operator
workflow thread via `thread_id`. Mirrors`session.schema.json`.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Direction](https://docs.rs/enum.Direction.html)
- Message direction relative to the platform.
Mirrors `message.schema.json#/properties/direction`.
- [Participant](https://docs.rs/enum.ParticipantType.html)- Type
- Participant role discriminator.
Mirrors `participant.schema.json#/properties/type`(`user`|`ai-agent`|`human-agent`).
- [Platform](https://docs.rs/enum.Platform.html)
- The channel on which a conversation takes place.
Mirrors `conversation.schema.json#/properties/platform`.
- [Session](https://docs.rs/enum.SessionStatus.html)- Status
- Lifecycle status of a session.
Mirrors `session.schema.json#/properties/status`.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [CITATION_](https://docs.rs/constant.CITATION_SNIPPET_MAX_CHARS.html)- SNIPPET_ - MAX_ - CHARS
- Max characters of a chunk to carry as a citation `snippet`. Bounds the size of the`eventual_response`payload; the full chunk lives in the KB.

# Checkpoint in smooth_operator - Rust

[.](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/tool/struct.ToolRegistry.html)

`ToolRegistry`This is the load-bearing proof of consumption: it builds an

    self: &[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<Self>,
    task: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    sub_config: &[SubAgentConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.SubAgentConfig.html),
) -> [DelegationHandle](https://docs.rs/struct.DelegationHandle.html)

Spawn a sub-agent to work on the given task in a background tokio task.

The sub-agent inherits the parent’s `LlmConfig`. If `sub_config.inherit_tools`
is true, the parent’s tool registry is cloned (tool `Arc`s are shared, hooks are not).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator_core/agent.rs.html#833-1117)#### pub async fn [run_with_channel](https://docs.rs#method.run_with_channel)(
    &self,
    user_message: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    tx: [UnboundedSender](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.52.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tokio/sync/mpsc/unbounded/struct.UnboundedSender.html)<[AgentEvent](https://docs.rs/enum.AgentEvent.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/type.Result.html)<[Conversation](https://docs.rs/conversation/struct.Conversation.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator_core/agent.rs.html#833-1117)

#### pub async fn [run_with_channel](https://docs.rs#method.run_with_channel)(
    &self,
    user_message: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    tx: [UnboundedSender](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.52.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tokio/sync/mpsc/unbounded/struct.UnboundedSender.html)<[AgentEvent](https://docs.rs/enum.AgentEvent.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/type.Result.html)<[Conversation](https://docs.rs/conversation/struct.Conversation.html)>

Run the agent loop with streaming LLM responses, sending events through a channel.

This is the streaming counterpart to `run()`. Instead of using the closure-based
event handler, all events (including token deltas) are sent through the provided
`mpsc::UnboundedSender`. This is designed for TUI consumption.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-2)Errors

Returns error if the LLM call or tool execution fails fatally.

# smooth_operator::embedding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/embedding/index.html

## Expand description

Text → vector embedding — the shared seam for dense retrieval.

Both the Postgres adapter (pgvector knowledge base) and the ingestion
pipeline need to turn text into dense vectors, and they must agree byte-for-
byte: a document embedded at ingest time and a query embedded at retrieval
time only land close together if they went through the *same* projection.
This module is that one shared home, so the two consumers can never drift.

- `Embedder`- `Embedder::dim`
- `DeterministicEmbedder`- **default**. A stable hash-based pseudo-embedding (FNV-1a token hashing, L2-normalized, no network), so conformance tests are reproducible with zero API calls and zero cost. Dimension is configurable; the Postgres schema defaults to- **1024**(mirrors smooai’s- `knowledge_vectors embedding vector(1024)`, Voyage- `voyage-3-large`shape).
- `cosine_similarity`

Provider-backed embedders live with their consumer: the Postgres adapter’s
`GatewayEmbedder` (an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` HTTP client over the
SmooAI LiteLLM gateway) implements this same [ Embedder](https://docs.rs/trait.Embedder.html) trait but stays in
the adapter crate so

`core` keeps no heavy HTTP dependency on the dense path.[§](https://docs.rs#dimension-decision)Dimension decision

Voyage (`voyage-3-large`, 1024-d) is the production north-star (it backs
smooai’s `knowledge_vectors`), but Voyage is *not* exposed on the LiteLLM
gateway. The gateway does expose OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` (1536-d).
Rather than couple the column width to whichever embedder happens to be
configured, the vector dimension is a first-class parameter — the Postgres
adapter takes its `vector(N)` column width from `embedder.dim()`, so dense
retrieval is always dimension-consistent.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Deterministic](https://docs.rs/struct.DeterministicEmbedder.html)- Embedder
- Deterministic, network-free pseudo-embedder.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Input](https://docs.rs/enum.InputType.html)- Type
- Whether an embedding is for a document being stored or a search query.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_DIM.html)- EMBEDDING_ - DIM
- Default embedding dimension (Voyage `voyage-3-large`shape; mirrors smooai’s`knowledge_vectors embedding vector(1024)`).

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Embedder](https://docs.rs/trait.Embedder.html)
- Turn text into dense vectors. Implementations must return one vector per
input string, each of length `Embedder::dim`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [cosine_](https://docs.rs/fn.cosine_similarity.html)- similarity
- Cosine similarity of two equal-length vectors.

---

# DeterministicEmbedder in smooth_operator::embedding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/embedding/struct.DeterministicEmbedder.html

`pub struct DeterministicEmbedder { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Deterministic, network-free pseudo-embedder.

Produces a stable vector from the text via a token-hashing bag-of-words projection, then L2-normalizes it so cosine distance is well-behaved. Same text → same vector, always. This makes pgvector retrieval (and ingestion) tests reproducible without any external service: a document and a query that share salient tokens land close together in the projected space.

# smooth_operator::rerank - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/rerank/index.html

## Expand description

Reranking — the optional post-retrieval reorder stage (feature gap G8).

Hybrid retrieval (dense pgvector ∪ sparse `tsvector` BM25 → Reciprocal Rank
Fusion) gives a good top-K, but the fusion score is a *rank* signal, not a
relevance score against the actual query. A reranker takes that candidate set
and reorders it with a sharper query↔candidate relevance model, so the best
few float to the top before they reach the model’s context window.

This is a **seam**, opt-in and behavior-preserving by default:

- `Reranker`- `rerank(query, candidates, top_k)`returns a reordered, truncated- `Vec<KnowledgeResult>`.
- `NoopReranker`- `top_k`candidates unchanged, so wiring it in never changes existing behavior.
- `LexicalReranker`- `DeterministicEmbedder`

[§](https://docs.rs#where-a-gatewayreranker-plugs-in)Where a `GatewayReranker` plugs in

A production reranker (Cohere `rerank-3`, Voyage `rerank-2`) is a cross-
encoder behind a paid API. It would live in the **adapter** crate (alongside
`GatewayEmbedder`), as a `GatewayReranker` that `impl Reranker` and POSTs
`{ query, documents, top_n }` to the gateway’s `/v1/rerank` endpoint, reading
the returned `index → relevance_score` and reordering accordingly. It is
deliberately *not* implemented here: `core` keeps no paid-API dependency on
the rerank path, exactly as it keeps `GatewayEmbedder` out of the dense path.
Swap it in by constructing the runtime / `KnowledgeSearchTool` with
`Some(Arc::new(GatewayReranker::from_env()?))` instead of the default.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Lexical](https://docs.rs/struct.LexicalReranker.html)- Reranker
- Deterministic, network-free lexical reranker.
- [Noop](https://docs.rs/struct.NoopReranker.html)- Reranker
- Identity reranker — the behavior-preserving default.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Reranker](https://docs.rs/trait.Reranker.html)
- Reorder retrieval candidates by query relevance, returning the top `top_k`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [apply_](https://docs.rs/fn.apply_optional_rerank.html)- optional_ - rerank
- Apply an optional reranker to a freshly-retrieved candidate set.

---

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/rerank.rs.html#46-51)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/rerank.rs.html#46-51)

Rerank `candidates` against `query`, returning at most `top_k`, best
first. Implementations must be total: an empty candidate set yields an
empty result, and `top_k == 0` yields an empty result.

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# MessagePage in smooth_operator::adapter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/adapter/struct.MessagePage.html

## Expand description

A page of messages, newest-or-oldest-first per the adapter’s contract,
with an opaque cursor for the next page (`None` when exhausted).

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.messages)

`messages: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Message](https://docs.rs/domain/struct.Message.html)>[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.next_cursor)

`next_cursor: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>Opaque cursor to pass back as `MessageQuery::cursor` for the next page.

# advance_after_verdict in smooth_operator::agent_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/agent_config/fn.advance_after_verdict.html

```
pub fn advance_after_verdict(
    workflow: &
```
[ConversationWorkflow](https://docs.rs/struct.ConversationWorkflow.html),
    current_step_id: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>,
    verdict: [WorkflowJudgeVerdict](https://docs.rs/enum.WorkflowJudgeVerdict.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>## Expand description

Compute the tracked step id after a judge verdict. `Yes` advances (to
[ next_step](https://docs.rs/fn.next_step.html), or stays put on a terminal step); every other verdict stays on
the current step. Never freezes: an unresolvable pointer resolves to the
first step. Returns

`None` only for an empty workflow.

---

# next_step in smooth_operator::agent_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/agent_config/fn.next_step.html

```
pub fn next_step<'a>(
    workflow: &'a
```
[ConversationWorkflow](https://docs.rs/struct.ConversationWorkflow.html),
    current: &[ConversationWorkflowStep](https://docs.rs/struct.ConversationWorkflowStep.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&'a [ConversationWorkflowStep](https://docs.rs/struct.ConversationWorkflowStep.html)>## Expand description

The step to advance to once `current` is satisfied. Preference order:

- explicit `current.next`if it resolves to a known step id,
- the element immediately following `current`,
- `None`— workflow complete (terminal step).

# resolve_current_step in smooth_operator::agent_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/agent_config/fn.resolve_current_step.html

```
pub fn resolve_current_step<'a>(
    workflow: &'a
```
[ConversationWorkflow](https://docs.rs/struct.ConversationWorkflow.html),
    current_step_id: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>,
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&'a [ConversationWorkflowStep](https://docs.rs/struct.ConversationWorkflowStep.html)>## Expand description

Resolve the current step for a `(workflow, pointer)` pair.

- Pointer matches a step id → that step.
- Pointer empty / unknown → the first step (fresh start).
- Empty workflow → `None`.

# tool_auth_refusal in smooth_operator::agent_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/agent_config/fn.tool_auth_refusal.html

```
pub fn tool_auth_refusal(
    tool_name: &
```
[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    level: [AuthLevel](https://docs.rs/enum.AuthLevel.html),
    visibility: [Visibility](https://docs.rs/enum.Visibility.html),
    session_authenticated: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>## Expand description

Decide whether a tool call is allowed given its required auth level, the
agent’s visibility, and whether the session is identity-verified. Mirrors
`tool-execution.ts` (lines ~145-190). `None` (allow) or `Some(message)` (the
reference refusal the model is shown). Callers gate ONLY when `level != AuthLevel::None` AND the tool supports auth requirements.

- internal agent → auto-satisfied (both `end_user`and`admin`);
- public + `admin`→ refuse (admin tools never run on public agents);
- public + `end_user`→ satisfied only when the session is identity-verified, else refuse asking for verification (the OTP flow is host wiring behind this seam — here the default is fail-closed).

---

# AgentBehaviorConfig in smooth_operator::agent_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/agent_config/struct.AgentBehaviorConfig.html

```
pub struct AgentBehaviorConfig {
    pub visibility:
```
[Visibility](https://docs.rs/enum.Visibility.html),
    pub instructions: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    pub persona: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    pub greeting: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    pub conversation_workflow: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ConversationWorkflow](https://docs.rs/struct.ConversationWorkflow.html)>,
    pub enabled_tools: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[EnabledTool](https://docs.rs/struct.EnabledTool.html)>,
}## Expand description

The resolved per-agent behavior knobs. Every field is optional so a partial
or malformed `agents` row degrades cleanly to the org default.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.visibility)

`visibility: `[Visibility](https://docs.rs/enum.Visibility.html)Where the agent is reachable — gates tool auth. Defaults to `Public`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.instructions)

`instructions: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>`instructions.prompt` — the agent’s system prompt / persona. When present
it overrides the org default persona for this agent’s conversations.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.persona)

`persona: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>`personality.persona` — an optional custom-persona addendum appended to
the system prompt.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.greeting)

`greeting: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>`greeting` — an optional opening line, injected into the prompt only on
the first turn of a conversation (see [`greeting_section`]).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.conversation_workflow)

`conversation_workflow: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ConversationWorkflow](https://docs.rs/struct.ConversationWorkflow.html)>`conversation_workflow` — the optional stepped guided flow. `None` (or a
malformed / empty-steps value) means the agent runs freeform.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.enabled_tools)

`enabled_tools: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[EnabledTool](https://docs.rs/struct.EnabledTool.html)>`tool_config.enabledTools` — a tool allow-list. When non-empty, this
agent’s turns are restricted to the `enabled == true` entries’ `tool_id`
(empty ⇒ the full server tool set). Unknown tool ids are ignored.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

`true` when the row carried nothing usable — the runner should stay on the
org default persona and take no workflow path.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#313-330)#### pub fn [system_prompt](https://docs.rs#method.system_prompt)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#313-330)

#### pub fn [system_prompt](https://docs.rs#method.system_prompt)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>

Build the per-agent system prompt from `instructions` (+ optional persona),
or `None` when there are no `instructions` to anchor it.

`None` is the signal to fall back to the org default persona — a bare
persona with no instructions is not enough to define an agent. The greeting
is handled separately ([ greeting_section](https://docs.rs/struct.AgentBehaviorConfig.html#method.greeting_section)) because
it is injected first-turn-only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#336-345)#### pub fn [greeting_section](https://docs.rs#method.greeting_section)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#336-345)

#### pub fn [greeting_section](https://docs.rs#method.greeting_section)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>

The `<GreetingAwareness>` prompt section, or `None` when no greeting is set.
The caller injects it only on the FIRST turn (empty prior history), so the
agent opens with it once. Mirrors the sibling lanes’ first-turn greeting.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#352-363)#### pub fn [enabled_tool_ids](https://docs.rs#method.enabled_tool_ids)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>>

The enabled tool-id allow-list, or `None` when unrestricted (no
`tool_config` / empty `enabledTools` ⇒ the full server tool set).
`Some(ids)` restricts the turn to those snake_case ids (`enabled == true`
entries only); unknown ids simply match nothing.

#### pub fn [tool_configs](https://docs.rs#method.tool_configs)(&self) -> [HashMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/map/struct.HashMap.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)>

The per-tool `config` object delivered to a tool at execution (the
`enabledTools` entry’s `config`), for every entry that carries one. Empty
when no tool has config. Mirrors `registry.ts`’s `toolSpecificConfig`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#397-447)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#397-447)

Parse from the raw `agents`-row jsonb / text columns, tolerating any
malformed shape (a bad value drops just that field — never an error).

- `instructions`— jsonb- `{ "prompt": string }`,
- `personality`— jsonb- `{ "persona"?: string, ... }`,
- `greeting`— text,
- `conversation_workflow`— jsonb- `{ goal, steps: [...] }`,
- `tool_config`— jsonb- `{ enabledTools: [{ toolId, enabled, authLevel, config }] }`,
- `visibility`— text- `public`|- `internal`(defaults- `public`).

# AgentConfigResolver in smooth_operator::agent_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/agent_config/trait.AgentConfigResolver.html

`pub trait AgentConfigResolver: `[Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html) {
    // Required method
    fn [resolve](https://docs.rs#tymethod.resolve)<'life0, 'life1, 'async_trait>(
        &'life0 self,
        agent_id: &'life1 [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    ) -> [Pin](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/pin/struct.Pin.html)<[Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn [Future](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/future/future/trait.Future.html)<Output = [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[AgentBehaviorConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.AgentBehaviorConfig.html)>> + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + 'async_trait>>
       where Self: 'async_trait,
             'life0: 'async_trait,
             'life1: 'async_trait;
}## Expand description

Seam for resolving an agent’s [ AgentBehaviorConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.AgentBehaviorConfig.html) by

`agent_id`.The ws protocol’s `create_conversation_session` carries only an agent UUID, so
per-agent config is looked up **server-side by id**. Implemented by the host
(backed by the monorepo `agents` table). Returning `None` means “no per-agent
config” — the runner falls back to the org default persona, exactly as before
this seam existed. Matches the sibling lanes’ `AgentConfigResolver.resolve`.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#642)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#642)

The per-agent behavior config for `agent_id`, or `None` when the agent is
unknown / has no usable config.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

# AuthGateHook in smooth_operator::agent_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/agent_config/struct.AuthGateHook.html

`pub struct AuthGateHook { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ ToolHook](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/tool/trait.ToolHook.html) that blocks a tool call whose configured

[isn’t satisfied — the operator-side analog of](https://docs.rs/enum.AuthLevel.html)

`AuthLevel``tool-execution.ts`’s auth gate. A
blocked call surfaces the reference refusal to the model (the engine turns a
`pre_call` error into the tool result), so the tool never executes.Only tools in [ auth_supporting_tools](https://docs.rs/struct.AuthGateHook.html#structfield.auth_supporting_tools) are gated
(the

`supportsAuthRequirement` flag; empty ⇒ the hook is inert — every current
built-in). The identity-verified `session_authenticated` bit is the seam a
host with an OTP flow flips; the reference server leaves it fail-closed
(`false`).## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#191-228)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-AuthGateHook)### impl [AuthGateHook](https://docs.rs/struct.AuthGateHook.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#191-228)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-AuthGateHook)

### impl [AuthGateHook](https://docs.rs/struct.AuthGateHook.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#195-208)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#195-208)

Build the gate from an agent’s resolved auth levels + visibility. Only the
tools in `auth_supporting_tools` are ever gated.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#215-217)#### pub fn [otp_refused_tool](https://docs.rs#method.otp_refused_tool)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/agent_config.rs.html#215-217)

#### pub fn [otp_refused_tool](https://docs.rs#method.otp_refused_tool)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>

The name of an `end_user` tool this hook refused for lack of a verified
session during the turn, if any. `Some(tool)` is the server’s signal to
offer OTP; `None` means nothing OTP-remediable was blocked. Cheap to poll
on a clone of the hook the server retained before installing it.

`intent: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)What the agent should try to accomplish on this step.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.criteria)

`criteria: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Objective criteria the judge evaluates to decide whether the step was satisfied this turn.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.next)

`next: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>Step id to advance to once criteria are met. Omit / empty on terminal steps (advancement then falls through to the next array element).

# EnabledTool in smooth_operator::agent_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/agent_config/struct.EnabledTool.html

```
pub struct EnabledTool {
    pub tool_id:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub enabled: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub auth_level: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub config: [Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html),
}## Expand description

One entry in `tool_config.enabledTools` (the monorepo `AgentToolConfig`
shape). `auth_level` / `config` are preserved on the parsed type for
downstream hosts even though the reference server doesn’t act on them yet.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.tool_id)

`tool_id: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)The tool’s snake_case id (e.g. `knowledge_search`).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.enabled)

`enabled: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Whether the tool is enabled for this agent.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.auth_level)

`auth_level: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Auth level the tool requires (`none` by default). Carried for hosts.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.config)

`config: `[Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)Opaque per-tool config. Carried for hosts.

# StaticAgentConfigResolver in smooth_operator::agent_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/agent_config/struct.StaticAgentConfigResolver.html

`pub struct StaticAgentConfigResolver { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Static map resolver (`agentId` → config), for tests and DB-free hosts. The
empty default is the server’s no-op resolver (every agent → `None`), so the
reference/OSS server stays on its org-default behavior.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# Visibility in smooth_operator::agent_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/agent_config/enum.Visibility.html

```
pub enum Visibility {
    Public,
    Internal,
}
```
## Expand description

Where an agent is reachable (monorepo `AgentVisibility`). `internal` agents
run behind an authenticated dashboard session, so their tool auth is
auto-satisfied; `public` agents (the default) are widget-embeddable.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Public)

### Public

Public widget-embeddable agent (the default).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Internal)

### Internal

Internal dashboard-only agent (authenticated session).

# NoAuthVerifier in smooth_operator::auth - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/auth/struct.NoAuthVerifier.html

`pub struct NoAuthVerifier { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

**Dev-only** verifier: returns a fixed `Admin` principal for *any* token
(including none). Reachable only via an explicit `AUTH_MODE=none`
([ AuthConfig::from_env](https://docs.rs/struct.AuthConfig.html#method.from_env)) so it can never be the silent production default.

# ConnectorConfig in smooth_operator::connector_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/connector_config/struct.ConnectorConfig.html

```
pub struct ConnectorConfig {
    pub id:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub org_id: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub name: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub kind: [ConnectorKind](https://docs.rs/enum.ConnectorKind.html),
    pub config: [Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html),
    pub enabled: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub created_at: [DateTime](https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.45/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/chrono/datetime/struct.DateTime.html)<[Utc](https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.45/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/chrono/offset/utc/struct.Utc.html)>,
    pub updated_at: [DateTime](https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.45/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/chrono/datetime/struct.DateTime.html)<[Utc](https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.45/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/chrono/offset/utc/struct.Utc.html)>,
}## Expand description

A persisted, org-scoped connector configuration.

The `config` payload is connector-kind-specific and free-form so a new
connector kind needs no schema migration. For `github` it carries
`owner` / `repo` and optionally `ref` / `include` / `visibility`; for `web`
a `url`; for `file` a `path`. The optional ** auth_ref** names the secret to
resolve at index time — the secret value is

**never**stored here.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.id)

`id: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Stable id (uuid v4), unique within the org.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.org_id)

`org_id: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)The owning organization — every store operation is scoped to this.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.name)

`name: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Human-readable name for the connector.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.kind)

`kind: `[ConnectorKind](https://docs.rs/enum.ConnectorKind.html)The source kind.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.config)

`config: `[Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)Kind-specific configuration (owner/repo/url/path/include/ref/…). May carry
an `auth_ref` naming a secret; never the secret itself.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.enabled)

`enabled: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Whether the connector is active (a disabled connector is configured but
won’t be auto-indexed by a scheduler; manual `/index` still works).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.created_at)

`created_at: `[DateTime](https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.45/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/chrono/datetime/struct.DateTime.html)<[Utc](https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.45/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/chrono/offset/utc/struct.Utc.html)>When the config row was created.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.updated_at)

`updated_at: `[DateTime](https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.45/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/chrono/datetime/struct.DateTime.html)<[Utc](https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.45/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/chrono/offset/utc/struct.Utc.html)>When the config row was last updated.

# ConnectorKind in smooth_operator::connector_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/connector_config/enum.ConnectorKind.html

```
pub enum ConnectorKind {
    Github,
    Web,
    File,
}
```
## Expand description

The kind of source a [ ConnectorConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ConnectorConfig.html) describes. Mirrors the built-in

`smooth_operator_ingestion` connectors (`github` / `web` / `file`); an
unknown wire value is rejected at the API boundary with a clean 400.## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Github)

### Github

A GitHub repository (prose/code/issues) — `GithubConnector`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Web)

### Web

A single public web URL — `WebConnector`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.File)

### File

A local file tree — `FileConnector`.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Stamp a numeric boost onto a Document’s metadata (builder). A non-finite
or negative value is normalized so the stamp is always a sane, parseable
multiplier.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/curation.rs.html#102)#### pub const [DOCUMENT_SET_KEY](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.DOCUMENT_SET_KEY): &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html) = "document_set"

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/curation.rs.html#102)

#### pub const [DOCUMENT_SET_KEY](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.DOCUMENT_SET_KEY): &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html) = "document_set"

The document-metadata key under which set membership is stamped. The
value is a **comma-separated** list (e.g. `"alpha"` or `"alpha,beta"`).

The document-metadata key under which the numeric boost is stamped (a
stringified `f32`, e.g. `"3.0"`).

Parse the document-set list from a `document_set` metadata value:
comma-split, trim each name, drop empties. Returns an empty vec when the
key is absent or holds only whitespace/commas.

# RetrievalFilter in smooth_operator::curation - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/curation/struct.RetrievalFilter.html

```
pub struct RetrievalFilter {
    pub document_sets:
```
[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>>,
    pub metadata_eq: [HashMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/map/struct.HashMap.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
}## Expand description

A query-time retrieval filter: scope results to named document sets and/or require metadata equalities.

- `document_sets: None`⇒- **no set scoping**(every document is eligible — the current/default behavior).- `Some([])`⇒ scope to- *no*set (matches nothing);- `Some(["alpha"])`⇒ only documents in set- `"alpha"`; a doc in- **any**of the listed sets matches (union).
- `metadata_eq`⇒ every- `(key, value)`must be present and equal in the document’s stamped metadata (logical AND across the map). Empty ⇒ no metadata constraint.

An all-default `RetrievalFilter` ([ RetrievalFilter::none](https://docs.rs/struct.RetrievalFilter.html#method.none)) matches every
document — the no-op that preserves current retrieval behavior.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.document_sets)

`document_sets: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>>Scope to documents in any of these sets. `None` ⇒ unscoped (all docs).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.metadata_eq)

`metadata_eq: `[HashMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/map/struct.HashMap.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>Require these `key == value` metadata equalities (all must hold).

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

The no-op filter: no set scoping, no metadata constraint — matches every document (preserves default retrieval behavior).

Scope retrieval to the given document sets (a doc in any of them matches).

Add a required metadata equality (builder).

# Citation in smooth_operator::domain - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/smooth_operator/domain/struct.Citation.html

```
pub struct Citation {
    pub id:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub title: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub url: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    pub snippet: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub score: [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html),
}## Expand description

A source the agent used to ground its answer.

Mirrors `spec/domain/citation.schema.json` and the optional `citations`
array on the terminal `eventual_response` event. Each citation points back at
one retrieved knowledge-base document — the chunk the model read plus enough
metadata to render an attribution link.

Citations are built from the
[ KnowledgeResult](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/knowledge/struct.KnowledgeResult.html)s that actually
grounded a turn (see

[/](https://docs.rs/struct.Citation.html#method.from_knowledge_result)

`Citation::from_knowledge_result`[):](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)

`From<KnowledgeResult>``id` ← `document_id`, `title` ← `source`,
`url` ← `source` when it is an `http(s)` URL (the GitHub blob/issue URL the
connector stamps onto the document’s `source` at ingest — see
`docs/CONNECTORS.md`) else `None`, `snippet` ← the chunk truncated for
display, `score` ← `score`.## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.id)

`id: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Stable identifier of the cited source document (the knowledge-base
`document_id`). Used to deduplicate citations within a turn.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.title)

`title: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Human-readable label for the source — the document’s source path or, for web-sourced docs, the URL/title.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.url)

`url: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>Canonical link to the source, when one exists. For GitHub-sourced
documents this is the blob/issue URL stamped onto the document’s `source`
at ingest. `None` for sources with no web location (e.g. uploaded files).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.snippet)

`snippet: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)The retrieved chunk text that grounded the answer, truncated for display.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.score)

`score: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html)Relevance score of this source for the turn’s query (the knowledge-base similarity score). Higher is more relevant.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/domain.rs.html#293-301)#### pub fn [from_knowledge_result](https://docs.rs#method.from_knowledge_result)(result: &[KnowledgeResult](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/knowledge/struct.KnowledgeResult.html)) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator/domain.rs.html#293-301)

#### pub fn [from_knowledge_result](https://docs.rs#method.from_knowledge_result)(result: &[KnowledgeResult](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/knowledge/struct.KnowledgeResult.html)) -> Self

Build a [ Citation](https://docs.rs/struct.Citation.html) from a knowledge-base

[.](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/knowledge/struct.KnowledgeResult.html)

`KnowledgeResult`- `id`←- `document_id`
- `title`←- `source`
- `url`←- `source`when it parses as an- `http`/- `https`URL (the GitHub blob/issue URL the connector stamps onto- `Document.source`at ingest —- `docs/CONNECTORS.md`), otherwise- `None`(e.g. a local- `policies/x.md`path has no web location).
- `snippet`←- `chunk`, truncated to- `CITATION_SNIPPET_MAX_CHARS`
- `score`←- `score`
